canonical_statement: TRUSS is designed to generate agent skills whose functional claims and safety properties are checked with both static artifact inspection and controlled runtime evidence before admission.
TRUSS supports task-conditioned generation, where the downstream task is known, and task-agnostic generation, where the downstream task is hidden and evaluation uses held-out tasks.
Functional effectiveness is defined as the expected utility gain produced by a skill relative to running the same agent and task with an empty skill.
For each safety property, TRUSS defines safety risk as the expected indicator that the evaluated skill violates that property under the evaluation distribution.
The stated optimization objective trades functional effectiveness against the mean risk across applicable safety properties using a weighting parameter.
The framework is an iterative Generator, Checker, and Refiner loop in which static findings and runtime failures are linked back to the exact skill candidate that produced them.
The Generator produces a complete candidate skill package, including the instruction document and executable resources needed for the skill.

Before checking, TRUSS freezes the candidate package, records its generation regime and source provenance, assigns a content digest, and binds findings, traces, and revisions to that exact candidate identity.

Static functional inspection extracts each claimed usage condition and observable effect and links the claim to source evidence or open-world knowledge, with source evidence taking precedence when available.

When a functional criterion cannot be resolved statically, TRUSS turns the remaining uncertainty into an executable runtime obligation; contradictory or untestable criteria are returned for refinement.
P1 Control Integrity protects task control from instruction manipulation; the paper assigns this property to static evidence.
P2 Access Boundary limits capability use to authorized data scope; the paper assigns this property to static evidence.
P3 Execution Integrity requires trusted provenance for executable behavior; the paper assigns this property to static evidence.
P4 Lifecycle Isolation keeps state within the authorized task lifecycle; the paper assigns this property to both evidence.
P5 Resource Boundedness bounds environmental effects by scenario budgets; the paper assigns this property to both evidence.
P6 Evidence Integrity aligns reported results with execution evidence; the paper assigns this property to runtime evidence.
P7 Authority Integrity binds consequential actions to valid authority; the paper assigns this property to runtime evidence.
P8 Composition Integrity preserves trust across composed agent components; the paper assigns this property to both evidence.
P9 Transaction Safety restricts external transactions to declared policy; the paper assigns this property to both evidence.
The static safety scope is derived from both declared behavior and implemented capabilities, so implementation details can expand the inspection scope beyond the skill description.
A candidate passes the static gate only for its exact content digest, after all static criteria are discharged and each remaining runtime obligation is specified well enough to execute.

Runtime checking uses a Controllable Execution Environment with a disposable workspace, synthetic task data, read-only skill mounting, excluded host resources, disabled direct command networking, and brokered mock services.

An intermediate breaker evaluates every requested action before dispatch; rejected requests return a structured blocked result and remain in the execution trace rather than disappearing from the evidence record.

Each tool interaction is normalized into an execution event that preserves the original call identity, returned observation, broker decision, causal parent, scenario identity, and skill digest, and the trace continues through cleanup and final environment state.

Functional runtime evaluation uses an outcome oracle to inspect resulting task state and completion claims and compares the skill-enabled run with an empty-skill run under the same task and agent conditions.

For runtime safety, policy-violating requests count as violations even when the broker blocks them; admitted actions are checked by observers, missing observer coverage leaves the obligation unresolved, and synthetic canaries can track protected information lineage.

The Function and Safety Record gives the Refiner an evidence-bound revision specification: static findings point to criteria and artifact spans, runtime findings point to requests and trace positions, and functional failures compare expected with observed state.
After a revision, TRUSS assigns a new content digest, repeats static inspection, and, if admitted, executes fresh runtime checks specific to that revised digest.

TRUSS certifies a candidate only when required functional outcomes are established and all applicable safety obligations are resolved under the evaluated scenarios; exhausting the revision budget returns an uncertified candidate with its residual record.
The RQ1 vulnerability-detection evaluation uses 84 matched clean/injected SkillInject pairs, yielding 168 blinded skill artifacts.
The RQ2 repair evaluation uses all 155 SkillSafetyBench cases with the benchmark task verifier and attack verifier.
The RQ3 automated-generation evaluation uses all 187 SkillGenBench tasks drawn from three source types.
On the 168 SkillInject artifacts, TRUSS achieved 100% precision, compared with 81.55% for the Static Checker and 44.64% for the Intermediate LLM Checker.
On the 168 SkillInject artifacts, TRUSS achieved 100% recall, compared with 94.05% for the Static Checker and 19.05% for the Intermediate LLM Checker.
On the 168 SkillInject artifacts, TRUSS achieved 100% F1 score, compared with 87.36% for the Static Checker and 26.69% for the Intermediate LLM Checker.
With Codex + GPT-5.5, repair reduced attack success rate from 38.71% to 19.35% on SkillSafetyBench.

canonical_statement: On 187 SkillGenBench tasks, task effectiveness was 52.94% with TRUSS, 29.95% with the LLM Generator, and 17.11% with no skills.
Relative to no skills, the reported absolute task-effectiveness improvement was 35.83 percentage points for TRUSS and 12.83 percentage points for the LLM Generator.
On the SkillGenBench controlled safety probes, mean security pass rate was 100% for TRUSS, 75.40% for the LLM Generator, and 50.80% with no skills.

canonical_statement: The authors conclude that combining static inspection with execution evidence can expose failures that artifact-only review misses and can provide traceable evidence for skill refinement and admission.

The paper reports residual attack success after repair and a large difference in safe task completion between executor configurations, and states that runtime certification remains sensitive to scenario coverage and executor behavior.

The main paper does not isolate the contribution of static inspection, runtime execution, and refinement within the full TRUSS pipeline; the evaluation text says component ablation is reported separately.
The authors identify broader scenario diversity and broader property-observer coverage as future directions for the verification framework.
